newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Giordano reports growth in tough China.
newsitem.headline: Giordano reports growth in tough China.

text.p: Giordano International Ltd said on Friday its China retail business posted a 7.6 percent growth in sales and 22 percent rise in net profit in 1996 despite a particularly difficult year for its operation there last year.
"The improved sales performance was derived mostly from the higher productivity on the sales floor and higher efficiency of the sales operation," the company said in a statement.

All Giordano's 11 franchisee shops in Shanghai were closed in March 1996 and soon thereafter, many more retail shops were closed in other parts of the country. Most of these shops were reopened later with the exception of Shanghai, it said.
"We are in the process of applying to open new outlets in Shanghai," Giordano's chairman Peter Lau told a news conference.

Giordano's flagship China store in Beijing was closed in 1994 by the Chinese authorities due to licensing problems. Most analysts believed, however, it was related with founder Jimmy Lai's vitriolic comments about Chinese premier Li Peng in his Next Magazine.
Lau said Giordano has some wholesale business in Shanghai but still has no presence in Beijing.
There were a lot of changes in the Chinese market and some of them were probably unique Giordano factors. Most were due to market fluctuation, the chairman said.
"We are not totally stopping in China, we have some good growth in China in 1996 and probably also in 1997," he added.
The Hong Kong retailer had 130 outlets in China as of April 30 compared to 120 by the end of 1996, an executive director of Giordano Terry Ng said.

Profits from the group's manufacturing operation in China fell in 1996, partly due to disruptions and delays in production and shipment schedules of its manufacturing facilities in Guangdong province, the company also said.
Lau said these problems, which had been addressed by the company, were mainly technical and procedural problems.
"These are commonly faced by Hong Kong manufacturers in China," Lau said.
The chairman said the company continued to receive proposals from investors in Hong Kong, China and overseas for the purchase of a stake in Giordano.

"We have not decided whether we need a partner and if yes, we will look for a strategic investor which would provide a concrete help to Giordano's business," he said, adding the company currently did not have any funding needs.
Giordano called off a planned placement of new shares with five mainland Chinese companies in April after the five failed to complete the deal.
